name: Effelsberg 100-m Radio Telescope
place: Effelsberg, Bad Münstereifel, Eifel (Ahr Hills), North Rhine-Westphalia
description: A fully steerable 100-metre radio telescope operated by the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy. It observes pulsars, gas and dust clouds, star-forming regions, magnetic fields and jets from black holes.
highlights: Inaugurated on 12 May 1971 and in full operation in 1972.
For 29 years it was the largest fully steerable radio telescope on Earth, until the Green Bank Telescope in 2000.
It serves as a station in international radio-telescope arrays that produce the sharpest cosmic images.
